title.japanese: {自|じ}{動|どう}{詞|し}と{他|た}{動|どう}{詞|し}

body:
## Two Verbs for One Event

English uses the same verb whether a door opens by itself or somebody opens it. Japanese uses two:

- ⟦ドア→ドア：00773_doa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{開|あ}く→開く：00689_aku⟧ — The door opens.
- ⟦ドア→ドア：00773_doa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧ — (Someone) opens the door.

⟦{開|あ}く→開く：00689_aku⟧ is a ⟦{自動詞|じどうし}→自動詞：10977_jidoushi⟧, an **intransitive** verb: its subject, marked with が, is the thing that changes. ⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧ is a ⟦{他動詞|たどうし}→他動詞：10418_tadoushi⟧, a **transitive** verb: its subject acts on an object marked with ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧. The two verbs share a root and differ only in the ending, and Japanese has hundreds of such pairs. Learning them as pairs, together with their particles, is one of the best investments an intermediate learner can make.

## Why the Choice Matters

The intransitive verb presents the change itself, with no doer in view; the transitive verb presents somebody causing it.

- ⟦お{湯|ゆ}→お湯：02518_oyu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{沸|わ}いた→沸く：01122_waku⟧ — The water has boiled.
- ⟦お{湯|ゆ}→お湯：02518_oyu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{沸|わ}かした→沸かす：01105_wakasu⟧ — I boiled some water.

Japanese often prefers the intransitive verb when the doer is unimportant or when the speaker would rather not point at anyone. Announcements say ⟦{電車|でんしゃ}→電車：00522_densha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{止|と}まりました→止まる：00555_tomaru⟧ (the train has stopped) and ⟦{会議|かいぎ}→会議：00710_kaigi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{始|はじ}まります→始まる：00841_hajimaru⟧ (the meeting will begin). After an accident, ⟦コップ→コップ：00862_koppu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{割|わ}れた→割れる：00907_wareru⟧ (the glass broke) reports what happened, while ⟦コップ→コップ：00862_koppu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{割|わ}った→割る：02334_waru⟧ (I broke the glass) admits responsibility.

The most common learner error is mixing the two halves of a pair: ⟦ドア→ドア：00773_doa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}く→開く：00689_aku⟧ and ⟦{電気|でんき}→電気：09780_denki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{消|き}える→消える：02520_kieru⟧ are wrong, because ⟦{開|あ}く→開く：00689_aku⟧ and ⟦{消|き}える→消える：02520_kieru⟧ cannot take an object. Keep the particle attached to the verb when you memorize it: ⟦ドア→ドア：00773_doa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{開|あ}く→開く：00689_aku⟧, ⟦ドア→ドア：00773_doa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧.

## Patterns in the Endings

The pairs are not random. Most follow one of a few patterns, and once you know the patterns you can often guess the partner of a verb you meet for the first time.

| Pattern (intransitive / transitive) | Intransitive | Transitive | More pairs |
|------|------|------|------|
| -aru / -eru | ⟦{上|あ}がる→上がる：00615_agaru⟧ (to rise) | ⟦{上|あ}げる→上げる：02443_ageru⟧ (to raise) | ⟦{下|さ}がる→下がる：01188_sagaru⟧／⟦{下|さ}げる→下げる：00807_sageru⟧, ⟦{閉|し}まる→閉まる：00754_shimaru⟧／⟦{閉|し}める→閉める：00485_shimeru⟧, ⟦{止|と}まる→止まる：00555_tomaru⟧／⟦{止|と}める→止める：00678_tomeru⟧, ⟦{決|き}まる→決まる：01233_kimaru⟧／⟦{決|き}める→決める：00858_kimeru⟧, ⟦{集|あつ}まる→集まる：01162_atsumaru⟧／⟦{集|あつ}める→集める：01170_atsumeru⟧, ⟦{始|はじ}まる→始まる：00841_hajimaru⟧／⟦{始|はじ}める→始める：00531_hajimeru⟧, ⟦{見|み}つかる→見つかる：01173_mitsukaru⟧／⟦{見|み}つける→見つける：01180_mitsukeru⟧, ⟦{変|か}わる→変わる：00714_kawaru⟧／⟦{変|か}える→変える：01089_kaeru⟧ |
| -u / -eru | ⟦{開|あ}く→開く：00689_aku⟧ (to open) | ⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧ (to open) | ⟦{付|つ}く→付く：01960_tsuku⟧／⟦{付|つ}ける→付ける：00761_tsukeru⟧, ⟦{届|とど}く→届く：00899_todoku⟧／⟦{届|とど}ける→届ける：01248_todokeru⟧, ⟦{立|た}つ→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧／⟦{立|た}てる→立てる：01196_tateru⟧, ⟦{建|た}つ→建つ：12544_tatsu⟧／⟦{建|た}てる→建てる：01189_tateru⟧, ⟦{育|そだ}つ→育つ：01951_sodatsu⟧／⟦{育|そだ}てる→育てる：01235_sodateru⟧, ⟦{続|つづ}く→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧／⟦{続|つづ}ける→続ける：01231_tsuzukeru⟧, ⟦{進|すす}む→進む：01225_susumu⟧／⟦{進|すす}める→進める：01949_susumeru⟧, ⟦{並|なら}ぶ→並ぶ：00605_narabu⟧／⟦{並|なら}べる→並べる：01091_naraberu⟧ |
| -reru / -su | ⟦{壊|こわ}れる→壊れる：00791_kowareru⟧ (to break) | ⟦{壊|こわ}す→壊す：01241_kowasu⟧ (to break) | ⟦{倒|たお}れる→倒れる：01160_taoreru⟧／⟦{倒|たお}す→倒す：01954_taosu⟧, ⟦{汚|よご}れる→汚れる：01293_yogoreru⟧／⟦{汚|よご}す→汚す：02327_yogosu⟧, ⟦{流|なが}れる→流れる：01969_nagareru⟧／⟦{流|なが}す→流す：01968_nagasu⟧, ⟦{隠|かく}れる→隠れる：02035_kakureru⟧／⟦{隠|かく}す→隠す：02034_kakusu⟧, ⟦{外|はず}れる→外れる：02395_hazureru⟧／⟦{外|はず}す→外す：02394_hazusu⟧, ⟦{離|はな}れる→離れる：02397_hanareru⟧／⟦{離|はな}す→離す：19372_hanasu⟧ |
| -eru / -su | ⟦{消|き}える→消える：02520_kieru⟧ (to go out) | ⟦{消|け}す→消す：00528_kesu⟧ (to turn off) | ⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧／⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧, ⟦{覚|さ}める→覚める：02058_sameru⟧／⟦{覚|さ}ます→覚ます：02057_samasu⟧, ⟦{冷|さ}める→冷める：02114_sameru⟧／⟦{冷|さ}ます→冷ます：02113_samasu⟧ |
| -eru / -yasu | ⟦{増|ふ}える→増える：01183_fueru⟧ (to increase) | ⟦{増|ふ}やす→増やす：02410_fuyasu⟧ (to increase) | ⟦{冷|ひ}える→冷える：01154_hieru⟧／⟦{冷|ひ}やす→冷やす：02403_hiyasu⟧, ⟦{燃|も}える→燃える：02312_moeru⟧／⟦{燃|も}やす→燃やす：02318_moyasu⟧ |
| -u / -asu | ⟦{動|うご}く→動く：00904_ugoku⟧ (to move) | ⟦{動|うご}かす→動かす：01885_ugokasu⟧ (to move) | ⟦{乾|かわ}く→乾く：00786_kawaku⟧／⟦{乾|かわ}かす→乾かす：01931_kawakasu⟧, ⟦{沸|わ}く→沸く：01122_waku⟧／⟦{沸|わ}かす→沸かす：01105_wakasu⟧, ⟦{飛|と}ぶ→飛ぶ：00759_tobu⟧／⟦{飛|と}ばす→飛ばす：02373_tobasu⟧, ⟦{減|へ}る→減る：01985_heru⟧／⟦{減|へ}らす→減らす：02414_herasu⟧, ⟦{鳴|な}る→鳴る：01143_naru⟧／⟦{鳴|な}らす→鳴らす：02381_narasu⟧ |
| -ru / -su | ⟦{直|なお}る→直る：00735_naoru⟧ (to get fixed) | ⟦{直|なお}す→直す：00869_naosu⟧ (to fix) | ⟦{治|なお}る→治る：19598_naoru⟧／⟦{治|なお}す→治す：19371_naosu⟧, ⟦{戻|もど}る→戻る：01117_modoru⟧／⟦{戻|もど}す→戻す：02317_modosu⟧, ⟦{回|まわ}る→回る：01150_mawaru⟧／⟦{回|まわ}す→回す：01158_mawasu⟧, ⟦{通|とお}る→通る：01243_tooru⟧／⟦{通|とお}す→通す：02300_toosu⟧, ⟦{残|のこ}る→残る：01187_nokoru⟧／⟦{残|のこ}す→残す：01975_nokosu⟧, ⟦{返|かえ}る→返る：29164_kaeru⟧／⟦{返|かえ}す→返す：09648_kaesu⟧, ⟦{渡|わた}る→渡る：02441_wataru⟧／⟦{渡|わた}す→渡す：02442_watasu⟧, ⟦{移|うつ}る→移る：01232_utsuru⟧／⟦{移|うつ}す→移す：10122_utsusu⟧ |
| -iru / -osu | ⟦{落|お}ちる→落ちる：01242_ochiru⟧ (to fall) | ⟦{落|お}とす→落とす：01246_otosu⟧ (to drop) | ⟦{起|お}きる→起きる：00521_okiru⟧／⟦{起|お}こす→起こす：01234_okosu⟧, ⟦{降|お}りる→降りる：00568_oriru⟧／⟦{降|お}ろす→降ろす：01923_orosu⟧, ⟦{過|す}ぎる→過ぎる：01219_sugiru⟧／⟦{過|す}ごす→過ごす：02062_sugosu⟧ |
| -eru / -u | ⟦{売|う}れる→売れる：02012_ureru⟧ (to sell well) | ⟦{売|う}る→売る：00906_uru⟧ (to sell) | ⟦{切|き}れる→切れる：01936_kireru⟧／⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧, ⟦{折|お}れる→折れる：01266_oreru⟧／⟦{折|お}る→折る：01263_oru⟧, ⟦{割|わ}れる→割れる：00907_wareru⟧／⟦{割|わ}る→割る：02334_waru⟧, ⟦{破|やぶ}れる→破れる：02322_yabureru⟧／⟦{破|やぶ}る→破る：02321_yaburu⟧, ⟦{抜|ぬ}ける→抜ける：02385_nukeru⟧／⟦{抜|ぬ}く→抜く：02384_nuku⟧, ⟦{焼|や}ける→焼ける：01138_yakeru⟧／⟦{焼|や}く→焼く：01123_yaku⟧, ⟦{取|と}れる→取れる：02376_toreru⟧／⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧ |

Three rules of thumb fall out of the table:

1. **An ending in す (⟦{消|け}す→消す：00528_kesu⟧, ⟦{増|ふ}やす→増やす：02410_fuyasu⟧, ⟦{動|うご}かす→動かす：01885_ugokasu⟧, ⟦{落|お}とす→落とす：01246_otosu⟧) is almost always transitive.** The す is the same causative idea found in ⟦させる→する：00392_suru⟧.
2. **An ending in ⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧ (⟦{閉|し}まる→閉まる：00754_shimaru⟧, ⟦{集|あつ}まる→集まる：01162_atsumaru⟧) is almost always intransitive.**
3. **An ending in える can go either way.** ⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧ is transitive, but ⟦{割|わ}れる→割れる：00907_wareru⟧ and ⟦{売|う}れる→売れる：02012_ureru⟧ are intransitive. This is the one pattern you cannot guess: learn each pair.

## One Form, Both Uses

A few common verbs work both ways without changing shape:

- ⟦{開|ひら}く→開く：01979_hiraku⟧ — ⟦ドア→ドア：00773_doa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{開|ひら}く→開く：01979_hiraku⟧ (the door opens) / ⟦{本|ほん}→本：00111_hon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|ひら}く→開く：01979_hiraku⟧ (to open a book)
- ⟦{閉|と}じる→閉じる：02303_tojiru⟧ — ⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{閉|と}じる→閉じる：02303_tojiru⟧ (the eyes close) / ⟦{目|め}を{閉|と}じる→目を閉じる：19363_mewotojiru⟧ (to close one's eyes)
- ⟦{吹|ふ}く→吹く：02445_fuku⟧ — ⟦{風|かぜ}→風：00641_kaze⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{吹|ふ}く→吹く：02445_fuku⟧ (the wind blows) / ⟦{笛|ふえ}→笛：03593_fue⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{吹|ふ}く→吹く：02445_fuku⟧ (to blow a whistle)
- ⟦{増|ま}す→増す：02422_masu⟧ — ⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ま}す→増す：02422_masu⟧ (the water rises) / ⟦{速度|そくど}→速度：03319_sokudo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{増|ま}す→増す：02422_masu⟧ (to increase speed)

## Verbs Without a Partner

Not every verb has a pair. ⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧, ⟦{読|よ}む→読む：00426_yomu⟧, ⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧, and ⟦{買|か}う→買う：00489_kau⟧ are transitive only; ⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧, ⟦{来|く}る→来る：00254_kuru⟧, ⟦{泳|およ}ぐ→泳ぐ：00545_oyogu⟧, ⟦{死|し}ぬ→死ぬ：00669_shinu⟧, ⟦{咲|さ}く→咲く：08150_saku⟧, and ⟦{泣|な}く→泣く：00655_naku⟧ are intransitive only. To make someone do these things, Japanese uses the causative form instead of a separate verb: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{野菜|やさい}→野菜：02265_yasai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べさせる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧ (to make a child eat vegetables), ⟦{妹|いもうと}→妹：00573_imouto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{泣|な}かせる→泣く：00655_naku⟧ (to make my sister cry).

Watch out for ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ after an intransitive verb of movement. In ⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧ (to walk along the road), ⟦{公園|こうえん}→公園：00581_kouen⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{走|はし}る→走る：00519_hashiru⟧ (to run through the park), and ⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧ (to leave the house), ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ marks the route or the point of departure, not an object being acted on. ⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧ and ⟦{走|はし}る→走る：00519_hashiru⟧ stay intransitive.

## Which State Are You Describing?

The pair also decides what 〜て⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧ means. With an intransitive verb of change, 〜て⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧ describes the resulting state; with a transitive verb, it describes an action in progress; and a transitive verb with 〜て⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧ describes a state that someone created on purpose.

- ⟦ドア→ドア：00773_doa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{開|あ}いている→開く：00689_aku⟧ — The door is open.
- ⟦ドア→ドア：00773_doa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}けている→開ける：00563_akeru⟧ — (Someone) is opening the door, or keeps it open.
- ⟦ドア→ドア：00773_doa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{開|あ}けてある→開ける：00563_akeru⟧ — The door has been left open (by someone, for a reason).

The helper verbs behind these forms are explained in [The Te-Form Helper Verbs](te-form-helpers.html).

## Tips for Learners

1. **Learn verbs in pairs, with their particles.** ⟦ドア→ドア：00773_doa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{開|あ}く→開く：00689_aku⟧／⟦ドア→ドア：00773_doa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧ is one item of vocabulary, not two.
2. **Use the endings as hints.** す means transitive; ⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧ means intransitive; える means look it up.
3. **Prefer the intransitive verb when nobody needs to be blamed or credited.** ⟦{電気|でんき}→電気：09780_denki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{消|き}えた→消える：02520_kieru⟧ is what you say when the lights go out; ⟦{電気|でんき}→電気：09780_denki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{消|け}した→消す：00528_kesu⟧ is what you say when you turned them off.
4. **Listen to announcements and shop staff.** Trains, stores, and offices use intransitive verbs constantly (⟦{間|ま}もなく→間もなく：02491_mamonaku⟧⟦ドア→ドア：00773_doa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{閉|し}まります→閉まる：00754_shimaru⟧ — the doors are about to close), and they are a good model for natural usage.
5. **Check the dictionary entry.** Every verb entry in this dictionary states whether it is transitive or intransitive and names its partner.
